A command for the human («❗ Выполнить») is a `bash` block (a run button), one command per block, no `&&` and no `;`: a chain is separate blocks. The command must work in both bash and PowerShell (the button runs it in the human's terminal): paths `D:/…`, not `/d/…` (PowerShell reads that as `D:\d\…`). Environment: Windows, Git Bash, Claude Code. A command longer than ~7 thousand characters (a commit message, a PR body, JSON) goes through a file (`-F`, `--body-file`, `--file`), not a heredoc. Arguments of the form `<ref>:<path>` (`git show`) need `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`. A project file is edited with Edit/Write, not `sed -i`/`perl -i`; a function with a regex or quotes — Read it whole and replace the block once; after a change of data shape — grep the usages; a literal `\uXXXX` — `perl -Mutf8 -CSD` with `\x5c`. At most 20 subagents at once (HTTP 429 breaks them all). A long call runs in the background, with an interim status to the human. The agent's token (`GH_TOKEN`) lacks `read:org`, which `gh pr edit` needs and the maintainer grants; meanwhile `gh api -X PATCH repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<N> -F body=@<file>`. `act.mjs` refuses an agent's shell and login: the maintainer runs it in their own terminal.

Language: new text written into the repository and onto GitHub — artifacts, code, comments, commits, PRs, issues — is English; Russian is used in the chat with the maintainer. Exceptions: Russian as data where the design requires it (Russian variants of bench items, SL-K03, BN-M04); history (old Russian specs, archived Changes, `design/`) is replaced by the Changes that touch it, never translated; files generated by WARRANT keep the language WARRANT writes them in; the marker «❗ Выполнить» is a fixed token addressed to the maintainer, in the chat and in PRs.

The maintainer's acts — merging a PR (the merge is the approval; GitHub's approve is not asked — PRs are opened under the maintainer's account, which cannot approve its own), activating a waiver, editing policy paths (`.github/workflows/**`, `.warrant/local/**`), deciding (an UNKNOWN, a `question`, a WARRANT question), repository settings and token scopes, files and tags outside `act.mjs` (a freeze tag of `design-next`), starting a session from a chip or restarting one — are never performed by the agent. A start is requested by the coordinator's chip, a restart in the session's own chat; any other act by a comment on the PR or issue it concerns: first line the marker `<!-- act: <kind> … -->` (skill `slice`), then what and why, the executor (session title and `claude://` link) and the one command where there is one — a merge, a waiver activation and a policy-path edit are `node <own worktree>/.claude/skills/slice/act.mjs merge <N>` · `waiver <change> <WAV>` · `patch <change> <file>` (a patch outside the repository), after its `--dry-run` passes — and tells the coordinator; only the coordinator writes the maintainer's commands into its chat, as its queue of «❗ Выполнить» blocks. `act.mjs` acts and verifies, or refuses with the reason and changes nothing; the agent reads the result itself (the commit, the waiver, the merge) and never asks the maintainer whether an act is done.

Project process. Every change of code and spec is an OpenSpec Change under WARRANT (schema warrant-sdd), from intent to archive in three PRs — spec, impl, archive; their steps are in the skill `slice`, file `.claude/skills/slice/change.md`, and a session follows them as written. The state of a Change is `warrant status`, the gates of a transition `warrant verify <change>`; a `warrant` error names its fix in `hint` — follow it. A session runs `warrant` commands that name a Change only on its own Change; the coordinator, and a judge of another's PR, only those that leave nothing in the repository.

Records (`.warrant/changes/**`), evidence, waivers, Runs and `openspec/specs/**` are written only by `warrant`; never edit them by hand, never call `openspec archive`. In a Change, the agent edits files of the repository only inside the `write_scope` of the active Run (what `warrant` and a git merge write are not its edits): `specify` the artifacts; `implement` narrowed with `--scope` to the source and test paths its design names plus `openspec/changes/<change>/**`. Never bypass a guard `deny` through the shell — narrow the work or ask the maintainer. A review subagent reads with the file tools and runs no shell command but `warrant run submit`; the session puts into its prompt what it needs from GitHub.

Parallel work (`design-next` SL-T08). An AREA is one spec and the prefix of its REQ/SCN ids. The AREAs of a Change are declared in `Where:` of its issue before `warrant init change`; after it an AREA is added only by a maintainer's `[decision]` naming the Change and the AREA, except `AR`, which a `skip_specs` Change (it declares none) adds itself when it needs an UNKNOWN. A Change holds its AREAs from `init` until its archive-PR is merged (or it is `ABANDONED`); one Change holds an AREA at a time, a second waits. At most three Changes are in implementation at once, from the first commit of the impl-PR until its merge. A fix of a red `main` (`fix-main-<issue>`) is exempt from the cap and from every AREA hold. One worktree and one session per Change; its three branches are made there in turn, each from fresh `origin/main`. Two parallel Changes never share a source path; files shared by several modules belong to the skeleton of the slice, and a later change of one is a separate small Change. What is held and what may start is computed by `node .claude/skills/slice/status.mjs`; after `init` a session runs it on its Change, and on a collision stops and asks on the umbrella.

Decision log. An umbrella comment whose first line starts with `[decision]` (the maintainer's, posted by the coordinator or, quoting the answer, by the session the maintainer answered), `[scope]` or `[broadcast]` binds the sessions it touches; the session acts on it, then acknowledges it by a reply on the umbrella (outside a slice: on its issue) that links it and names the Change. `[incident]` records a failure. Before `SPECIFIED` and before asking for a merge a session runs `status.mjs <change>`, reads what it lists — the entries it has not acknowledged and the comments of its own issue newer than its last push — and brings its work in line first. A slice decision that changes an open PR stops its merge: the coordinator turns the PR to draft, turns its auto-merge off and comments `⛔ Do not merge — <decision URL>`; a draft PR is never merged.

PRs. A spec-PR is offered only with `SPECIFIED` as its last commit; an impl-PR ends with `VERIFYING`, after an implementation review (skill `code-review`) stated in its body. Before a push that opens or updates a PR the owner runs `node .claude/skills/slice/judge.mjs` and pushes only when it reports no violation of the PR. The merge is a merge commit by the maintainer and is the approval; it is requested once, in the act queue (rule `maintainer-acts`), when no check has failed. A PR is owned by the session that opened it, and only the owner watches it: it binds the PR in the desktop app with auto-fix on (or tells the maintainer its CI is not watched; CI is never polled), starts `node .claude/skills/slice/wait-pr.mjs <N>` in the background right after the push that makes it wait for the maintainer, acts on its outcome, and starts its watchers again when it resumes.

Questions. A question of the spec is an UNKNOWN, decided by the maintainer's comment in the spec-PR; an implementation question, a change the spec review asks for after `SPECIFIED`, and a spec change after approval are `I-N` rows in `design.md` with the maintainer's decision.

Architecture (`design-next` ST-A01…ST-A04): at the end of every wave and on a trigger of ST-A02 the coordinator runs an architecture audit of `src/` against `design-next` into `design-next/reviews/`, grilled with the maintainer; an accepted finding that can be checked mechanically becomes a fitness test, the others a rule with an ID; a refactor is a separate Change that changes no behaviour.

The maintainer is `roles.maintainer` in `.warrant/warrant.json`. Commit and push go to your own branch; `main`, and `gh pr merge` except `--disable-auto`, are the maintainer's only.

Work is recorded where the event happens; there is no log file, and where we are is computed (`warrant status`, `git log`, `gh pr list`, `gh issue list`, skill `slice`). A task of a Change is `[x]` in `tasks.md`; a cancelled or moved task is removed, with an `I-N` row giving the reason and a link. Work without a Change is a commit and a PR that touches no policy path (`.warrant/local/**`, `.warrant/warrant.lock.json`, `.github/workflows/**`); one that does is a Change.

Issues. LATTICE debt outside the current Change (a defect, an idea, something deferred) is a GitHub issue the agent opens itself and names in its report; in code `#N`. Title `<prefix>: <what>` (`s0`…`s4`, `sw`, `design`, `infra`); body "Why:" a source link, "Where:" the Change, slice or trigger; a Change issue also "Depends on:", in the milestone of its slice — or of the slice it unblocks, else in none. Labels: one type — `bug` · `enhancement` · `question` — and one priority — `P1` blocks the slice or the honesty of the process · `P2` before the slice closes · `P3` some day. A process failure is an issue labelled `process` with "Root cause" and "Prevention", opened by the session that sees it.

Closing, the first that applies: a Change issue by its archive-PR (`Closes #N` there, not in the spec- or impl-PR); a `process` issue when its prevention is in place as a rule, a test or a setting, not when the failure is fixed; a `question` by the maintainer's answer, linked; any other issue by the PR that fixes it (`Closes #N` there). A duplicate gets the label `duplicate` and a link; a refusal the label `wontfix` and the reason. `status.mjs` lists the open issues whose condition looks met; the coordinator closes them.

A WARRANT defect, gap or idea is an issue in `Homasters-max/SRA` the agent opens itself: title `<area>: <what>` (`guard`, `cli`, `ci`, `records`, `docs`), one label `bug` · `enhancement` · `question`, body "Found in:" a LATTICE link and the WARRANT version, "What happened", "Expected" — facts about WARRANT only, the repository is public. It is named `Homasters-max/SRA#N` and linked from the LATTICE issue that waits on it.

Slices. A slice is a GitHub milestone and its umbrella issue: plan, list of Changes, decision log. Each Change is one session in its own worktree, started from its issue; it reads its issue, the `design-next` IDs it implements and the merged specs it depends on, not the context of other Changes. The coordinator session holds the slice — dispatch, review, the queue of the maintainer's acts, decision log (skill `slice`, "Coordinator") — and never writes a Change's code. A red `main` (a failed `test` run on `main`, or `warrant validate` failing on `origin/main`) is a `bug` `P1` issue `infra: main red — <failing test or error code>`, opened by the first session that sees it; while it is open no other Change is dispatched and only its fix is merged — a Change `fix-main-<issue>` whose issue the coordinator opens and whose session it offers. At the end of every wave, next to the architecture audit, the coordinator runs the retro: the `process` issues of the wave, summed up on the umbrella and grilled with the maintainer into a rule, a test or a setting.
